metadata.title: Trace Every Number to Its Source
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week10/term2-week10-video-content.md (Week 10); narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-28)
metadata.note: STEM/learning film, hai Plain register on the ai-explainer chassis. Thesis: keep a master number sheet — value, source, status — and a do-not-use list; it shows where a number came from, not whether the source was right, and a derived number is fine if labelled derived. Worked example: Week 10 article counts (~81,000, 10,055, 10,049 traced; 71,000 unsourced, derived by subtraction — shown only as unsourced/derived). On-screen numbers appear in the Week 10 source; the Your Turn size (five) is Janvi's supplied task.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about tracing every number in a document back to where it came from. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine.

props.command: My paper has collected numbers over months of drafts. How do I check where each one came from?
props.segment: Trace Every Number to Its Source.
output: Put every number in one sheet
Record each one's source and status
Flag any number without a source

beats.role_note: A paper page with numbers floating up from it, all equally bold; caption 'they all look equally solid'.
beats.narration_text: A paper collects numbers over months of drafts. Some come from data. Some come from a quick calculation. After a while, they all look equally solid.
beats.visual_intent: A paper page with numbers floating up from it, all equally bold; caption 'they all look equally solid'.

beats.role_note: Master number sheet with columns: value · source · status.
beats.narration_text: The fix is a master number sheet. Every number gets a row: the value, where it came from, and whether that source still says so.
beats.visual_intent: Master number sheet with columns: value · source · status.

beats.role_note: Rows filling: ~81,000 · substring run · ✓ / 10,055 · exact-match run · ✓ / 10,049 · after 6 duplicates · ✓.
beats.narration_text: In our paper, about 81,000 traced to substring matching, 10,055 to the exact-match run, and 10,049 to the count after six duplicates were removed.
beats.visual_intent: Rows filling: ~81,000 · substring run · ✓ / 10,055 · exact-match run · ✓ / 10,049 · after 6 duplicates · ✓.

beats.role_note: Row 71,000 · source '—' · status 'derived: ~81,000 − ~10,000'; 'written down as if measured'.
beats.narration_text: 71,000 traced to nothing. It was a subtraction, about 81,000 minus about 10,000, written down as if it had been measured.
beats.visual_intent: Row 71,000 · source '—' · status 'derived: ~81,000 − ~10,000'; 'written down as if measured'.

beats.role_note: 'do not use' list card (71,000 struck); search icon over the whole paper.
beats.narration_text: Keep a do-not-use list too. Retired numbers tend to come back in later edits, so the list lets you search for them before you submit.
beats.visual_intent: 'do not use' list card (71,000 struck); search icon over the whole paper.

beats.role_note: When NOT: 'source found ≠ source right'; 'derived is fine if labelled derived'.
beats.narration_text: What this doesn't do: it shows where a number came from, not whether the source was right. And a derived number isn't wrong; it just has to say it's derived.
beats.visual_intent: When NOT: 'source found ≠ source right'; 'derived is fine if labelled derived'.

show.event: derived is fine if labelled derived

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in the composer.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Pick five numbers from your latest report. For each one, write down its source. Any number without one goes on the list to check.

props.command: Here are five numbers from my report. For each, where did it come from, and which have no source?
props.segment: Trace Every Number to Its Source.
